questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly to describe an action that has no specific time mentioned?
options: I have visited London last year.
I have seen that movie three times.
I went to London yesterday.
I will visit London next week.
questions.answer: I have seen that movie three times.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form to complete the sentence: 'This book is _______ than the one I read last month.'
options: more interesting
interestinger
most interesting
interestingly

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the second conditional to talk about an unreal present situation?
options: If I had money, I would buy a car.
If I have money, I will buy a car.
If I had money, I will buy a car.
If I have money, I would buy a car.
questions.answer: If I had money, I would buy a car.

questions.question: Select the sentence that correctly uses a gerund as the subject of the sentence.
options: Swimming is good exercise.
To swim is good exercise.
Swim is good exercise.
Swam is good exercise.

questions.question: Which option uses the modal verb 'must' correctly to express a strong deduction?
options: He must be at home because his lights are on.
He must be at home because his lights are off.
He must have been at home because his lights are on.
He must have been at home because his lights are off.
questions.answer: He must be at home because his lights are on.

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the appropriate linker: '______ it was raining heavily, we decided to go for a walk.'
options: Because
Although
So
If

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past continuous to describe an action that was interrupted?
options: I was cooking when the phone rang.
I cooked when the phone rang.
I was cooking the phone rang.
I cooked the phone rang.
questions.answer: I was cooking when the phone rang.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the infinitive after the verb 'want'.
options: I want to go to the cinema.
I want going to the cinema.
I want go to the cinema.
I wanted to go to the cinema.
questions.answer: I want to go to the cinema.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the superlative form of the adjective 'happy'?
options: She is happier than her sister.
She is the happiest person in the room.
She is more happy than her sister.
She is very happy.
questions.answer: She is the happiest person in the room.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the third conditional to talk about a past unreal situation.
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I will pass the exam.
If I studied harder, I will have passed the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
